STATEMENT OF ACCUSED U/S 313 Cr.P.C.
23.

ARGUMENTS :
24.
Ld. Additional PP for State has argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the case of prosecution and their testimony has remained unrebutted.
It is argued that a young lady committed suicide within 4 years of marriage on account of cruelty and harassment caused by the accused persons for meeting the demands of dowry.
That on a combined reading of testimony of prosecution witnesses, offences U/s 498A/304B IPC are proved beyond any doubt.
It is argued that the accused has failed to rebut the presumption of law which proves his guilt, hence, he is liable to be held guilty.
FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 13 of 34 25.
On the contrary, the arguments of the Ld. Counsel appearing on behalf of the accused are two fold.
One, that the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses are inconsistent and have discrepancies that does not inspire confidence and also they do not support the case of prosecution in any manner.

Secondly, the main ingredients for the offences u/s 498A IPC and 304 B IPC have not been fulfilled as the prosecution has failed to prove the cruelty, demand of dowry by the accused and also the connection that the deceased was subjected to cruelty soon before her death by the accused.
It is argued that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case beyond its reasonable doubts so no presumption of law is attracted in this case.

Thus, on the aforesaid grounds, accused is entitled to be State vs Kuldeep Singh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40528451/
6 acquitted.
FINDINGS:
26. Arguments adduced by Ld.
Additional
PP for State and Ld.
Defence Counsel for the accused have been heard.
Evidences and documents on record perused carefully.

27. Before adverting to the facts of the present case, let the provisions of law be reproduced and the essential ingredient be enumerated that were required to be proved by the prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused persons.

FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 14 of 34 Section 304B of IPC says:
(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection, with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.

(2) ........
Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act says:
When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry,
the court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
Section 498A of IPC says:
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation-

For the purpose of this section, "Cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman;
FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 15 of 34 or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

State vs Kuldeep Singh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40528451/
7 28.
For proving the offence u/s 498A IPC, the prosecution was required to establish that woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment either by husband of the woman or by the relative of the husband.

For the purpose of this section, cruelty means that any willful conduct which is of such nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her or where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or is on account of failure by her to make that demand.
Cruelty for the purpose of constituting the offence u/s 498A IPC need not be physical.

Even mental torture in a given case would be case of cruelty within the meaning of section 498A IPC.
29.
The prosecution was required to prove the foundational facts before presumption of law is attracted and the burden of proof is shifted upon the accused persons.

Presumption under section 113B is a presumption of law that shall be raised only on proof of the following essentials;
FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 16 of 34 (i) The death of a woman must have been caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
( ii) Such death must have occurred with in seven years of her marriage.
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her relatives.
(iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
(v) The woman is subjected to such cruelty or harassment soon before her death.
30. Now this Court shall proceed on to deal with the five aspects / essentials enumerated above one by one to see whether the prosecution has been able to prove the same in the present case or not.
(i) The death of a woman must have been caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
31. It is the admitted case that the deceased Sapna died otherwise than under normal circumstances.

The postmortem report of deceased i.e. Ex.PW6/6 / Ex. A6 that has been duly proved on record proves the cause of death of the deceased Sapna as poisoning due to i.v. injection of a poisonous substance meaning thereby death was unnatural and was not under normal circumstances.

Hence,
this aspect stands duly established.
FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 17 of 34 (ii) Such death must have occurred with in seven years of her marriage.
32. It is also admitted that deceased Sapna died within 4 years of her marriage which means within seven years of her marriage, hence, this aspect also stands duly proved.

State vs Kuldeep Singh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40528451/
8
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her relatives and (iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
33. Both the aforesaid aspects are taken together being inter connected for the purpose of discussion and findings.
34. There are five material prosecution witnesses on the basis of which, case of prosecution lies.

Three of them are the family members of deceased i.e. PW-2 Sh. Tara Chand Bankar, PW-4 Ms.
Amruta Bankar and PW8 Sh. Rupesh Bankar.

Two are the the independent witnesses i.e. PW3 Sh.
Priju K. Johnson and PW7 Sh. Hari Shankar.
PW3 was the neighbour of the deceased and accused.
PW7 witnessed the marriage of accused and deceased.

It is to seen from the testimony of above witnesses as FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 18 of 34 to whether they have been able to establish the fact of causing of cruelty/harassment to deceased by accused persons for meeting demand of dowry which driven the deceased to commit suicide.
The testimony of such PWs is hereby dealt and appreciated separately as well as comparatively with other PWs as follows.
35. Now coming to the deposition of family members of the deceased that shall be discussed one by one.
Firstly, the father of the deceased namely Sh. Tarachand Bankar who has been examined as PW-2.
It is the PW2 on whose complaint the present prosecution initiated.
36. In his examination in chief, PW2 has nowhere stated that the accused demanded dowry from him or his family members nor it is stated that dowry was demanded from the deceased.
PW2 also did not state anywhere in his deposition that the deceased was harassed in any manner to meet the demands of dowry.
PW2 in his examination in chief admitted that deceased Sapna and the accused had love marriage.
During his cross examination, PW2 stated that he and his wife did not attend their marriage nor did they gave any dowry in the marriage.
PW2 further stated in his cross examination that no demand was made at the time of marriage.

During further cross examination,
PW2 admitted that during the lifetime of Sapna, neither he nor Sapna or any of his family members make any complaint against the accused to the police.
FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 19 of 34 37.

PW2 in his examination in chief stated that accused used to quarrel with Sapna and used to demand money from her sometimes Rs. 5,000/- or Rs. 10,000/- and prior to 1-2 months of her death she told PW2 about the demand of Rs. 50,000/- raised by the accused.
First and foremost, the aforesaid statement does not fall in the domain of demand of dowry.
Merely asking for money by husband from his wife does not amount to demand of dowry.

Secondly, PW2 has not given any particulars in terms of date and time or place whereby accused demanded such money from the deceased nor he could give any specific detail such as date and time when such demand was communicated by deceased to PW2.
This shows that vague allegation has been made by PW2 without any substance.
Above all, the aforesaid fact was not found recorded in the previous statement of PW2 that is Ex. PW2/B when the witness PW2 was confronted with the same during his cross examination.

State vs Kuldeep Singh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40528451/
9 38.
PW2 during his cross examination, stated that after coming to know about the marriage, neither he nor other family members accepted the marriage.

This statement of PW2 is completely contradictory to the stance taken by PW2 in his examination in chief where he stated that after having the knowledge about the marriage of his daughter Sapna from his other daughter Amruta, he alongwith his wife came to Delhi to meet them.

PW2 in his examination in chief stated about his visits to his deceased FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 20 of 34 daughter after her marriage but at no point of time, he was told about any harassment or demand of dowry either by the deceased or by sister of the deceased namely Amruta who was staying with deceased and accused.

It is also pertinent to note that whatever facts stated by PW2 in his examination in chief were not found recorded in the statement given to SDM Ex. PW2/B as the same was confronted during the cross examination of PW2.
Meaning thereby, PW2 introduced new facts and made improvement in his version recorded before the court as compared to his previous statement which loses the credence of his testimony.
The discussion above, clearly shows that the testimony of PW2 does not support the case of the prosecution in any manner nor does it inspire confidence of the court to be acted upon.
39. Now coming to the testimony of PW4, Ms. Amruta Bankar i.e. the sister of deceased Sapna.

This was the most important witness as she was residing with accused and deceased at the time of incident so no one other than PW4 was better to throw light on the relation between the accused and deceased.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that there is no allegation of causing harassment to the deceased Sapna was made by this witness in her testimony nor there is any allegation of demand of dowry made by her.
PW4 in her examination in chief stated that quarrel used to take place between Sapna and Kuldeep as Kuldeep had not informed his parents about the marriage.

PW4 further stated FIR No. 418/15 State vs Kuldeep Singh Page no. 21 of 34 that on 16.06.2013 also a fight took place between accused and the deceased at about 06.30 PM but she did not know the reason of the fight.
The aforesaid statements of PW4 do not refer to the quarrels due to demand of any dowry.
40. PW4 made a bald statement in her examination in chief that accused used to demand money from her sister.
Again no date or time or occasion has been mentioned by PW4 specifically when such demand was made.
As earlier observed in the previous paragraphs that the demand of money by the husband from his wife does not amount to demand of dowry by any stretch of imagination.
Except the above vague statement nothing else has been stated by PW4 in her examination in chief supporting the case of the prosecution in any manner.

During cross examination, PW4 was confronted with her previous statement Ex. PW4/A where the fact that accused used to demand money from her sister is not found recorded therein nor did she remember if such fact was stated to the police during the investigation.
In her cross examination, PW4 stated that she has deposited about Rs. 5,000/- in the account of accused at the instance of her sister.
When questioned about the account number of the accused, PW4 feigned ignorance.
In further cross examination, PW4 could not tell the date, month and year when she deposited the said amount in the account of the accused.

sentences.text: Noticeably this presumption as well is founded on the proof of cruelty or harassment of the woman dead for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the person charged with the offence.

The presumption as to dowry death thus would get activated only upon the proof of the fact that the deceased lady had been activated only upon the proof of the fact that the deceased lady had been subjected to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the accused and that too in the reasonable contiguity of death.

A conjoint reading of these three provisions, thus predicates the burden of the prosecution to unassailably substantiate the ingredients of the two offences by direct and convincing evidence so as to avail the presumption engrafted in section 113B of the Act against the accused.

Proof of cruelty or harassment by the husband or her relative or the person charged is thus the sine qua non to inspirit the statutory presumption, to draw the person charged within the coils thereof.

If the prosecution fails to demonstrate by cogent, coherent and persuasive evidence to prove such fact, the person accused of either of the above referred offences cannot be held guilty by taking refuge only of the presumption to cover up the shortfall in proof.

It is a settled proposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case on judicial file beyond reasonable doubt by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence.
The burden of proof of the version of the prosecution in a criminal trial throughout the trial is on the prosecution.
